info.title: OpenRouter Decisions (Supernala selection)
info.description: Reviewed selection of the Jev decision endpoint.

post.description: Fast typed decisions about content with TypeSafe's Jev: classify into options, score against levels, or get the probability a yes/no statement is true, with calibrated probabilities and confidence in about 0.1 s. Use it to classify, route, triage, screen, tag, or verify; act on high confidence and probability, and send uncertain answers to review. It cannot write text, extract values or locate things in images.

model.description: Jev model; `typesafe/jev-latest` follows the newest release.

state.description: The content every question refers to: text, or a JSON object or array of related context such as {"subject":...,"message":...}. Keep it focused; long state lowers accuracy.

instructions.description: What to decide, rate or evaluate.

criteria.description: choice: {option name: when it applies}. score: [lowest level, ..., highest level]. noul: optional {"true": ..., "false": ...}.

questions.description: Questions about `state`, each under a name you choose (letters, digits, underscores); answers come back under the same names. Ask several at once: it costs no more and is just as fast. Types: `choice` picks one option; `criteria` maps each option name to when it applies, e.g. {"billing":"Charges, refunds, invoices","bug":"Something is broken"}; the answer has `choice`, `confidence` and `probabilities` per option. `score` rates against ordered levels; `criteria` is a list of 1-10 level descriptions from lowest (0) up; the answer has the expected `score`, `confidence`, `legend` and `probabilities` per level. `noul` is a yes/no question or statement; optional `criteria` {"true":"what counts as yes","false":"what counts as no"}; the answer `noul` is the probability of yes (0-1). Jev returns typed answers only; it never writes text.

200.description: Answers keyed by question name, with the model used and token usage.
